entity.name: ARGUS — Agentic Research & Governance Unified System
entity.description: ARGUS is an open-source AI research organization building the world's first debate-native, multi-agent AI framework for evidence-based reasoning. Our flagship product, Argus Debate AI, eliminates hallucination through adversarial multi-agent debate, Bayesian aggregation, and full provenance tracking. We support 27+ LLM providers, 50+ tools, and publish all work under the MIT license. Our novel architecture — the Conceptual Debate Graph (C-DAG) and Evidence-Directed Debate Orchestration (EDDO) — represents original research contributions to AI reasoning, calibration, and governance. ARGUS is freely available for anyone to use, study, modify, and distribute.

projects.name: ARGUS — Argus Debate AI
projects.description: A debate-native, multi-agent AI framework for evidence-based reasoning with structured argumentation, decision-theoretic planning, and full provenance tracking. ARGUS implements the Research Debate Chain (RDC) — a novel approach that structures knowledge evaluation as multi-agent debates. Instead of single-pass LLM inference, ARGUS orchestrates Moderator, Specialist, Refuter, and Jury agents that gather evidence, generate rebuttals, and render verdicts through Bayesian aggregation. Key innovations include: (1) Conceptual Debate Graph (C-DAG) — a directed graph where propositions, evidence, and rebuttals are nodes with signed edges representing support/attack relationships; (2) Evidence-Directed Debate Orchestration (EDDO) — an algorithm managing multi-round debates with convergence detection; (3) Value of Information Planning using Expected Information Gain (EIG); (4) Full PROV-O compatible provenance tracking with SHA-256 hash-chain integrity. Supports 27+ LLM providers, 50+ tools, hybrid BM25+FAISS retrieval, and ships with a TUI, Streamlit sandbox, and REST API. Available on PyPI as argus-debate-ai.

channels.description: Support ARGUS directly through GitHub Sponsors. Accepts one-time and recurring monthly contributions via credit/debit card.

Fund ARGUS through Open Collective — transparent, publicly visible fund management. Accepts cards, PayPal, and bank transfers globally including from India. Ideal for corporate sponsors and international grant bodies.
Direct bank transfer available for institutional sponsors, grant bodies, and corporate donors. Please email support@argus-ai.dev with subject 'ARGUS Sponsorship' to receive bank details.

plans.name: Community Supporter
plans.description: Show your appreciation for ARGUS with a one-time contribution of any amount. Helps cover hosting, CI/CD pipelines, and PyPI infrastructure costs.

plans.name: Infrastructure Support (Monthly)
plans.description: Covers monthly infrastructure costs: GitHub Actions CI/CD, PyPI distribution, Docker Hub hosting, Streamlit Cloud sandbox, and API rate limits for running benchmark evaluations across FEVER, TruthfulQA, BoolQ, and ARC datasets.

plans.name: Core Developer Stipend (Monthly)
plans.description: Funds one core developer working part-time (20 hrs/week) on ARGUS — covering new LLM provider integrations, C-DAG improvements, EDDO convergence algorithms, documentation, and community support. This is the most impactful recurring plan.

plans.name: GPU Compute Grant (One-time)
plans.description: Funds a full multi-agent benchmark evaluation run across all 10 ARGUS evaluation datasets (1050+ samples each) and 5 global benchmarks (FEVER, SNLI, TruthfulQA, BoolQ, ARC) using GPU-accelerated FAISS dense retrieval and cross-encoder reranking. Results will be published openly as an arXiv paper.

plans.name: Research Fellowship Sponsorship (Yearly)
plans.description: Sponsors one full-time ARGUS research fellow for one year to work on novel extensions: quantum-inspired debate aggregation, federated multi-agent debate, and publishing the C-DAG and EDDO algorithms as peer-reviewed research. Fellow will contribute all work back to the open-source repository under MIT license.

plans.name: Corporate Sponsor
plans.description: For companies using ARGUS in production or research. Includes logo placement in README and documentation, priority issue resolution, and a quarterly call with the core team. Helps sustain long-term development of the framework.

history.description: Project inception year. Expenses covered personal compute, API credits for development and testing across 27+ LLM providers, and PyPI publishing costs. No external funding received.
